title: POC prioritization — multilingual model tradeoffs (AuroraEdge)
next_steps: Redwood to share tailored benchmark sheet + test harness link
Customer to provide 3 representative prompt sets (EN, ES, FR) by 2025-04-09
Schedule 90-min deep bench run with Devon week of 2025-04-14
Send security checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS) and initial Pricing estimate
action_items: Maya: Send benchmark template and quickstart repo link — due 2025-04-04
Devon: Prepare suggested model shortlist (quant/FP16/INT8 notes) and rough perf estimates — due 2025-04-08
Dr. Elena Ruiz: Share 3 sample prompt sets + volume estimates (tokens/month) — due 2025-04-09
Ravi: Confirm VPC requirements and available on-prem windows for pilot — due 2025-04-11
summary: Discovery / POC scoping call to define success criteria and shortlist open models for a multilingual extraction + summarization POC. Discussed workload sizing, latency targets, quality tradeoffs across model families, and operational constraints (VPC/on-prem, KMS, SOC2). Agreed next steps: share benchmark harness, customer to provide prompt sets, schedule bench run.
topics: POC goals and success criteria (accuracy thresholds, latency SLOs)
Workload sizing (concurrent users, tokens/month, peak patterns)
Model shortlist tradeoffs: instruction-tuned LLMs vs base + prompting
Multilingual coverage (English, Spanish, French priority; potential for German)
Benchmarks and metric definitions (EM, F1, BLEU-ish proxies, human eval plan)
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. We also have Devon from solutions engineering. quick roll call?
[00:09] Elena: Elena here, hi.
[00:11] Ravi: Ravi — SRE.
[00:13] Zoe: Zoe, product.
[00:15] Marco: Marco, CTO, i'm hopping in a bit late.
[00:20] Maya: Awesome. The goal today is to scope a short POC — multilingual extraction + summarization for AuroraEdge clinical notes pipeline. We want to pin success criteria, pick a model shortlist to bench, and agree timeline. Devon, want to frame the technical questions?
[00:34] Devon: Sure, thanks. Quick high level: what are your quality thresholds — like do you need X% exact entity extraction or is human-in-the-loop acceptable? And what are latency/throughput targets? also what's your target deployment — hosted API or VPC private?
[00:48] Elena: For extraction we'd like >= 88% F1 on our curated labels, and summarization should hit at least 4/5 on our human quality rubric — that's more subjective — but important is consistency across EN/ES/FR. Latency: p95 under 700ms for single short notes (~350 tokens). Peak patterns: up to 200 concurrent users during spikes, but avg more like 30.
[01:10] Zoe: And timeline — product wants a decision in 6 weeks, so POC needs to be quick: bench + 2-week pilot.
[01:19] Devon: Okay good. On model choices, we'll focus on open models — you mentioned you prefer open-source for auditability. We typically recommend 2-3 families for benching so we can compare quality vs cost. Thoughts on FP16 vs quantized runs?
[01:32] Elena: We care about on-prem later, so quantization will matter for Dedicated or Private. For hosted benching it's fine to run FP16. The risk is that quantization sometimes degrades multilingual quality, especially for Spanish medical jargon.
[01:47] Maya: Noted — we'll include quantized variants in the shortlist. Devon, can you talk through the shortlist proposal?
[01:53] Devon: Yeah. Proposed shortlist: 1) a large instruction-tuned LLM family A (strong instruction-following and summarization), 2) family B - more compact but strong multilingual base (good for quantization), 3) a base multilingual LLM with domain finetune on clinical tokens — we'll run both with prompt engineering and with a light finetune where feasible. We'll call out expected p95 latency on a c5-like GPU and also estimate tokens/sec.
[02:20] Ravi: For the POC we need estimates around GPU hours and network flows — if we end up doing Private we need to provision on-prem windows. We also need to validate KMS integration for keys and that logs go to our SIEM.
[02:33] Devon: We'll include an infra estimate. For context, a single bench run (10k prompts across 3 languages) usually takes 6-8 hours on a single A10 in FP16 without batching heavy. With batching and quantized int8 it can be faster. We'll include clear cost estimates.
[02:48] Zoe: How do you plan to score quality across languages? We need consistent metrics.
[02:52] Devon: We'll compute exact match and F1 for extraction. For summarization we'll do ROUGE/L BLEU proxies plus a small human eval sample per language (20-30 items) for rubric scoring. We'll surface regressions relative to your baseline.
[03:08] Elena: Baseline is current rule-based pipeline — it's okay but we want 20% lift in recall on key entities.
[03:14] Maya: Great. On security — we have SOC2 cert, SAML SSO, and we support KMS/HSM for Private deployments. We'll send the detailed security checklist. Any specifics we should call out?
[03:26] Ravi: Data residency — some transcripts must not leave EU for patients in EU. Also audit logs retention for 7 years.
[03:34] Devon: We can run regionally in eu-west for hosted, and private gives you full control. Audit logs and long-term retention are available as an add-on. We'll include that in pricing.
[03:44] Maya: Ok, let's align on success criteria so we can call the POC a win or fail. Elena?
[03:50] Elena: Win if extraction F1 >= 88% across EN/ES/FR, summarization rubric >= 4.0 avg, p95 latency < 700ms for typical note length, and integrated KMS + audit logs in place for the pilot. Also cost needs to be within ~30% of our target TCO for production — i'll share numbers.
[04:12] Devon: We'll map that to bench thresholds so the bench run can predict production. We'll also show model-variant fallbacks — like a smaller fallback model in case of latency spikes.
[04:23] Zoe: On fallback — does Redwood support automated routing between model tiers?
[04:27] Maya: Yes, smart routing and automatic fallback policies exist — we can configure per-route SLOs. We'll demo that if we get to the pilot.
[04:36] Marco: (joined) Sorry i'm late. Quick question: are you proposing we do instruction-tuned models or base models with prompt engineering? I care about maintainability.
[04:46] Devon: We recommend trying both in the short POC: instruction models for best out-of-the-box summarization; base models with light domain finetune or retrieval-augmented prompts sometimes have better extraction stability. We'll quantify maintenance overhead in notes.
[05:01] Elena: How about multilingual? Some families are trained heavily on English and degrade on ES/FR — we need parity.
[05:07] Devon: Correct. Family B is more multilingual robust but slightly worse on abstractive summarization in English. We'll include cross-lang deltas in the bench.
[05:17] Ravi: For workload sizing — our initial estimate: 1M tokens/month for core use, spikes up to 5M in a month. Concurrent users: steady 30, spikes 200. That should drive whether we go multi-GPU Dedicated.
[05:30] Devon: Thanks. So we'll prepare batch-sizing recommendations and autoscale policy suggestions.
[05:36] Maya: Let's talk timeline briefly: we propose bench setup this week, customer provides prompts by next Wednesday (2025-04-09), bench runs week of 4/14, results review 4/18, pilot starts 4/21 if bench looks good. Does that work?
[05:50] Zoe: Tight but doable.
[05:52] Elena: Works for me.
[05:53] Maya: Great. Now let's get a bit granular on the benchmark harness — Devon?
[05:56] Devon: The harness will run each model variant over the 3 language prompt sets. For extraction we'll calculate micro/macro F1, precision/recall, and per-entity confusion. For summarization we'll score with ROUGE-L and run the human rubrics. We will also measure latency distributions (p50,p95,p99) and token throughput. We'll run tests at two concurrency levels to simulate steady-state and peak. We'll also record memory / KV cache sizes because that impacts Dedicated sizing.
[06:22] Ravi: KV cache — you mean the attention cache? Our infra team uses that for cost estimates.
[06:26] Devon: Right, the decoders KV cache — sorry sometimes we say KV cash in notes — transcription quirks. That cache size grows with sequence length and influences GPU memory needs. We'll capture that.
[06:40] Elena: About evaluation — we also want a small blind human evaluation mixed in to capture hallucinations.
[06:45] Devon: Agreed — human eval to check hallucination rate, especially for domain-specific facts. We'll provide tooling to surface examples.
[06:52] Maya: A couple of pricing notes: hosted bench runs are charged per GPU-hour; Dedicated has a reserved monthly cost but predictable throughput. We'll share a ballpark to help decision.
[07:02] Zoe: On quantization, are there recommended quant profiles for Spanish clinical text?
[07:07] Devon: Not one-size-fits-all — but we'll try int8 QAT/awq variants and compare quality drop. We'll flag any tokens/wordpiece behavior in Spanish medical acronyms.
[07:20] Marco: For pilot, i'd prefer private deployment in our VPC if the security checks pass. We might also do hybrid: hosted for non-sensitive traffic, private for EU data.
[07:31] Maya: That's a common pattern. We'll include hybrid routing in the design doc.
[07:35] Elena: One red flag for us is reproducibility of results when moving from bench to quantized production. How do you handle drift?
[07:44] Devon: We'll produce model cards and deterministic seeds for bench runs; for quantized variants we'll run regression tests on your prompt set, plus Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce drift. We'll also provide evaluation monitors for early regression alerts.
[07:58] Ravi: For integration, we need SDK examples in Java and Go; our backend is Go-based.
[08:04] Devon: We have SDKs for Go and Python and REST; i'll link example code.
[08:09] Maya: Okay, quick check — does everyone have what they need on regulatory controls? We'll attach SOC2, data flow diagrams.
[08:17] Elena: Please include retention and deletion workflows — we need GDPR right to be forgotten flows documented.
[08:24] Maya: Will do. Devon, any follow-up on the model shortlist?
[08:27] Devon: Proposed models in the sheet: Model-A-Inst (large, strong EN summarization), Model-B-Multi (better ES/FR), Model-C-Base+Domain (finetune candidate). For each we'll test: FP16 hosted baseline, int8 and awq quant variants, and a small 2-epoch domain finetune where feasible. We'll also measure cost per 1k tokens for each variant.
[08:52] Zoe: Can you include a smaller micro model for fallback (faster but lower quality)?
[08:55] Devon: Yes, we'll include a micro model for fallback routing in the bench.
[08:58] Ravi: Regarding logs — we need raw request logs masked and separate redacted versions available for auditors.
[09:04] Maya: That is standard — we can provide masking and redaction pipelines, and store masked logs in your S3 or send to your SIEM.
[09:12] Elena: Let's also define what constitutes a failure after the POC — we need an objective pass/fail.
[09:18] Devon: We'll produce a POC scoring sheet that maps metrics to pass/fail: extraction F1 threshold, summarization human rubric, latency SLOs, security checklist items all need to be met or have approved workarounds.
[09:32] Marco: Cost question again — if dedicated reserved GPUs are too expensive, do you support autoscaling to cheaper preemptibles?
[09:40] Maya: We support burst to lower-cost capacity where appropriate, and routing policies can prefer cheaper model variants during low-priority periods. We'll show cost vs latency tradeoff.
[09:50] Elena: I'm worried about hallucinations in clinical context — how does Redwood help mitigate?
[09:56] Devon: Several approaches: retrieval augmentation, stricter prompt templates, and post-hoc fact-checking heuristics. We'll test RAG vs no-RAG in the bench so you can see hallucination delta.
[10:07] Zoe: Could the bench include a small patient-sim dataset with known facts for hallucination checks?
[10:11] Elena: yes, we'll provide sanitized examples for that.
[10:14] Maya: Perfect. We'll need 3 language sets, the sanitized patient-sim set, and ~10-15k prompts ideally for statistical power. If that's heavy, we can start with a smaller set and scale.
[10:26] Devon: For the bench harness link and quickstart, i'll post an initial repo and sample runner that runs locally or on Redwood infra. Link: https://redwood-internal.example.com/auroraedge-poc-harness (note: internal link). We'll also post a Google sheet with model variants: https://redwood-internal.sheets/auroraedge-benchmarks
[10:47] Ravi: (crosstalk) — can we also have cost per-1k tokens estimated for production at 1M tokens/month?
[10:52] Maya: Yes, Devon will produce cost estimates for each variant at your expected volumes and show per-token and monthly cost.
[10:58] Elena: On the human eval — can Redwood run the evaluation or do we need to coordinate externally?
[11:03] Devon: We can run the human eval with your reviewers or provide tooling and a small rater panel; either way we'll integrate results into the bench report.
[11:12] Zoe: One more practical question: who will be the day-to-day POC contact from Redwood?
[11:15] Maya: Devon will be your SE lead for the bench and will coordinate the runs; i'm the AE and will handle procurement/pricing and scheduling.
[11:23] Elena: Great. Any regulatory red flags?
[11:27] Devon: None immediate — once we get the sample prompts we can run a data flow review. We'll also do a short privacy assessment.
[11:35] Maya: Ok let's recap action items and timeline.
[11:38] Devon: I'll enumerate: share repo and harness (today/24h), prepare model shortlist and cost matrix (by 4/8), run bench once prompts are in (week of 4/14).
[11:48] Maya: AuroraEdge: deliver prompts + volume estimates by 4/9, confirm VPC/on-prem windows by 4/11.
[11:55] Zoe: We'll do that.
[11:57] Marco: Looking forward — thanks all.
[12:00] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and schedule.
[12:03] (call ends)
